title: Taiwan's Gyms Hit a Record as More People Work Out
summaryZh: 台灣健身房數量創新高，五年營收成長近四成。
summaryHi: ताइवान में जिम की संख्या रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर, कमाई भी तेज़ी से बढ़ी।
summaryEs: Taiwán bate su récord de gimnasios: más gente hace ejercicio y los ingresos suben.
summaryJa: 台湾のジム数が過去最多に、売上も5年で約4割増。
summaryKo: 대만 헬스장 수 사상 최다…5년 새 매출 약 40% 증가.
summaryEn: Taiwan now has a record 1,166 fitness centres, and gym revenue has grown about 40% in five years.
paragraphs: Taiwan's fitness boom shows no sign of slowing, with the number of gyms reaching a record high, according to Ministry of Finance statistics released this week.

The country had 1,127 fitness centres last year, a rise of 54.8 percent from 2020, and the figure climbed to 1,166 by the end of July. Gyms now account for 36 percent of all sports facilities, outnumbering golf courses, driving ranges and swimming pools. Their combined revenue reached NT$21.25 billion last year, topping NT$20 billion for the first time, and income in the first seven months of this year was up 12.6 percent.

The ministry linked the growth to rising health awareness. Because gyms focus on general fitness and are unaffected by weather, they appeal to a wide range of people. Operators have also broadened their services beyond equipment, adding group classes and personal training.

The industry is heavily concentrated in Taiwan's six special municipalities, which host three-quarters of all gyms and earn 82 percent of the revenue. Taipei leads with 181 centres, followed closely by Taichung with 173.

Yet rapid expansion has a downside. Taoyuan saw its number of gyms jump by more than 160 percent, but average revenue per centre fell by over 40 percent, which the ministry attributed to fiercer competition.
More and more people in Taiwan go to the gym. The country now has more gyms than ever before.
At the end of July this year, Taiwan had 1,166 gyms. Five years ago, it had far fewer. Last year, gyms made more than NT$21 billion. This is a new record.
Why do people like gyms? Many people want to be healthy. Also, you can go to the gym on rainy or very hot days. Many gyms now have group classes and personal trainers too.
Most gyms are in big cities. Taipei has the most, and Taichung is second. In Taoyuan, the number of gyms grew very fast. But there are many gyms there now, so each gym makes less money.
Taiwan's fitness industry is growing quickly, and the number of gyms has reached a record high, according to the Ministry of Finance.

There were 1,127 fitness centres last year, up almost 55 percent from 2020, and the number rose to 1,166 by the end of July this year. Gyms now make up 36 percent of all sports facilities in Taiwan, more than golf courses or swimming pools. Their total income last year was NT$21.25 billion, the first time it has passed NT$20 billion.

Officials say people are more interested in their health than before. Gyms are also popular because the weather does not matter: people can exercise indoors when it is raining or too hot. Many gyms now offer group classes and personal training as well as machines.
About three-quarters of all gyms are in Taiwan's six biggest cities. Taipei has the most, with 181, followed by Taichung with 173. The number of gyms in Taoyuan has more than doubled since 2020.
However, more gyms also mean more competition. In Taoyuan, the average income per gym has dropped by over 40 percent.
Taiwan's fitness boom shows no sign of slowing, with the number of gyms reaching a record high, according to Ministry of Finance statistics released this week.

The country had 1,127 fitness centres last year, a rise of 54.8 percent from 2020, and the figure climbed to 1,166 by the end of July. Gyms now account for 36 percent of all sports facilities, outnumbering golf courses, driving ranges and swimming pools. Their combined revenue reached NT$21.25 billion last year, topping NT$20 billion for the first time, and income in the first seven months of this year was up 12.6 percent.

The ministry linked the growth to rising health awareness. Because gyms focus on general fitness and are unaffected by weather, they appeal to a wide range of people. Operators have also broadened their services beyond equipment, adding group classes and personal training.

The industry is heavily concentrated in Taiwan's six special municipalities, which host three-quarters of all gyms and earn 82 percent of the revenue. Taipei leads with 181 centres, followed closely by Taichung with 173.

Yet rapid expansion has a downside. Taoyuan saw its number of gyms jump by more than 160 percent, but average revenue per centre fell by over 40 percent, which the ministry attributed to fiercer competition.
Taiwan's appetite for working out appears to be insatiable, with Ministry of Finance data showing that the number of gyms has climbed to an all-time high.

Fitness centres totalled 1,127 last year, 54.8 percent more than in 2020, and had reached 1,166 by the end of July, accounting for over a third of all sports facilities. Their revenue last year surpassed NT$20 billion for the first time, at NT$21.25 billion, and takings for the first seven months of 2026 were 12.6 percent higher year on year. The only setback came in 2021, when the pandemic dragged income down to NT$12.36 billion.

Officials attribute the surge to growing health consciousness, noting that gyms, unlike outdoor venues, operate regardless of the weather. Operators have also diversified, supplementing machines with group classes and personal coaching to attract new customers.

Geographically, the sector is highly concentrated: Taiwan's six special municipalities house roughly three-quarters of all gyms and generate 82 percent of revenue, with Taipei narrowly ahead of Taichung.

Expansion has nonetheless come at a price. Taoyuan, where gym numbers rose by more than 160 percent, has seen average revenue per centre slump by over 40 percent, a decline the ministry ascribed to intensifying competition.
Taiwan's fitness sector has expanded considerably in recent years, with official statistics indicating that the number of gyms has reached an unprecedented level.

According to the Ministry of Finance, there were 1,127 fitness centres last year, representing a 54.8 percent increase on 2020, and the total had risen further to 1,166 by the end of July. Gyms now constitute approximately 36 percent of all sports facilities. Their aggregate revenue exceeded NT$20 billion for the first time last year, while earnings for the first seven months of 2026 grew by 12.6 percent year on year.

The ministry attributed this growth primarily to heightened health awareness. A significant advantage of gyms is that they function irrespective of weather conditions, thereby appealing to a broad demographic. Furthermore, operators have diversified their offerings, introducing group classes and personal training alongside conventional equipment.

The industry is, however, geographically concentrated. The six special municipalities accommodate around three-quarters of all gyms and generate 82 percent of total revenue, with Taipei and Taichung dominating.

Rapid expansion has not been without consequences. In Taoyuan, gym numbers surged by over 160 percent, yet average revenue per centre declined by more than 40 percent, a trend the ministry attributed to increasingly fierce competition within a saturated market.
